user.title: Connect mimamori
user.description: Create a read-only token in mimamori under Settings → API tokens and paste it here. Use the HTTPS address of mimamori; plain HTTP only inside one Docker network, since the token would otherwise travel unencrypted.

data_description.url: As Home Assistant reaches it: the HTTPS address of your reverse proxy, or the container name and port 8000 inside one Docker network.
data_description.api_token: Starts with mmr_. It can only read, not change anything.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off only for a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: New API token for mimamori
reauth_confirm.description: mimamori at {url} no longer accepts the token; it was probably revoked. Create a new one under Settings → API tokens.

error.cannot_connect: mimamori could not be reached. Check the address and that Home Assistant can reach it.
error.invalid_auth: mimamori rejected the token. Check that it was copied completely and is not revoked.
error.invalid_token_format: This is not a mimamori API token. It starts with mmr_ and has 47 characters.
error.invalid_url: Enter a full HTTPS (or HTTP) address, including the scheme.
error.not_mimamori: The address answers, but not like mimamori v0.3.5 or newer. Check the address and update mimamori.
error.rate_limited: Too many wrong tokens: mimamori blocks this address for a few minutes. Wait, then try again.
error.redirected: The address redirects elsewhere. Enter the address it leads to, usually the HTTPS one.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.already_configured: This mimamori is already set up.

data_description.scan_seconds: Seconds between two requests. 60 is plenty: drives are checked hourly, status checks every minute or more.
